title: A Saved Listing Is Not Searchable Yet
description: A listing save commits to PostgreSQL, but CDC and search refresh take a few seconds. The seller's own page must show the saved data immediately; discovery can lag. Which policy fits?

options.text: Declare the database write failed when search returns no result.
options.explanation: Search lag does not prove the authoritative write failed; resubmitting may create duplicate work.

options.text: Use Elasticsearch as the only source of truth for the save.
options.explanation: That discards the designed authoritative store and does not address the separate refresh visibility boundary.

options.text: Serve the seller's page from PostgreSQL while the derived search index catches up.
options.explanation: Read-your-writes belongs on a source known to contain the save. Keeping discovery near-real-time avoids forcing refresh on every indexing operation.

options.text: Add replica shards to eliminate CDC delay.
options.explanation: Replicas copy indexed data; they cannot index a source change that has not arrived.
